title: The Time Is Drawing Near
description: The Time Is Drawing Near in Tonic Solfa to SOUTHWELL, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns from the Morningland (Paisley, 1911).
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Short Metre (6.6.8.6), and this page sets them to SOUTHWELL; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The time is draw-ing near, It can-not tar-ry long, When they who face the con-flict here, Shall join the glo-rious throng,

lines: When they who face the conflict here,
But let me hear, in winning tones,
That I may see the light serene
I may, like those who serve above,
May I, with those who see Thy face,

source: John Brownlie, Hymns from the Morningland (1911)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns from the Morningland; set to SOUTHWELL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
